title: Air India Launches Only Nonstop Delhi to Osaka Flights From February 2027
excerpt: Four weekly Boeing 787-8 services start on February 2, 2027, making Osaka Air India's second Japan destination after Tokyo Haneda and opening open-jaw Golden Route trips.
body:
• Air India will start four weekly nonstop flights between Delhi and Osaka Kansai on February 2, 2027, becoming the only airline on the route.
  • Flight AI360 leaves Delhi at 22:50 on Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays, arriving in Osaka at 09:50 the next morning; AI359 returns at 11:50, arriving in Delhi at 18:20.
  • The Boeing 787-8 will carry 259 passengers, with 18 full-flat Business Class beds and 241 Economy Class seats, and no Premium Economy cabin.
  • Reader utility: bookings are opening progressively now — book Delhi-Osaka from February 2, 2027 onward via Air India's website or app, and check Japan's eVISA rules before you pay.

Air India will launch nonstop flights between Delhi and Osaka on February 2, 2027, adding a second Japanese destination and the only direct link between the two cities. The airline announced the route on October 15, saying Osaka's Kansai International Airport will join Tokyo Haneda in its Japan network, according to Air India's official press release.

The service removes the need to connect through Tokyo, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur or another Asian hub to reach western Japan. For travellers heading to Osaka, Kyoto or Nara, that is a direct arrival in the Kansai region rather than a landing in the capital followed by a domestic flight or a long rail transfer.

Schedule, aircraft and booking

Air India will operate the route four times a week with a Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner. Flight AI360 departs Delhi at 22:50 on Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays and arrives in Osaka at 09:50 the following morning, local time. The return flight, AI359, departs Osaka at 11:50 on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays and arrives in Delhi at 18:20 the same day, Travel Trade Journal reported, matching the timings in Air India's announcement.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1l4thEo5Ftc

"Schedule, aircraft and booking Air India will operate the route four times a week with a Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner."

The overnight outbound timing is built for a morning arrival, with most of the first day still available in Osaka. The daytime return lands in Delhi in the early evening, which Air India says is designed to connect with onward flights across its domestic and international network through Delhi.

The 787-8 on this route has 18 full-flat beds in Business Class and 241 seats in Economy Class, for a total of 259 seats. Bookings are being opened progressively through Air India's website, mobile app, customer contact centre, airport ticketing offices and travel agents worldwide. Travellers should confirm the operating day carefully before locking in hotels or rail passes, because the flight does not run daily in either direction.

A second gateway after Tokyo Haneda

Osaka will become Air India's second destination in Japan after Tokyo Haneda, where the airline currently operates daily flights from Delhi and four weekly services from Mumbai. Adding Kansai therefore does not replace the Tokyo services; it widens the network to cover both eastern and western Japan with nonstop flights from India.

The addition also enables open-jaw itineraries. Passengers can fly into Osaka and return from Tokyo, or fly into Tokyo and return from Osaka, without backtracking to their arrival airport. Air India highlighted that flexibility for travellers following Japan's Golden Route, which links Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka in a single trip.

That matters for first-time visitors: a Golden Route holiday moves in one direction, and an open-jaw ticket matches that movement instead of forcing a return to the starting city.

Why Air India is adding Osaka now

Air India linked the launch to growing demand from Indian travellers and deepening economic, tourism and cultural ties between India and Japan. According to the Japan National Tourism Organization, cited in both Air India's release and Travel Trade Journal's coverage, Japan welcomed more than 315,000 Indian visitors in 2025. That was a 35 percent increase over 2024 and nearly 80 percent above pre-pandemic levels.

The growth reflects wider interest in Japan's leisure, cultural and culinary experiences alongside expanding business links. Osaka, Japan's second-largest metropolitan area, gives that demand a western gateway as well as a capital gateway.

What it means for diaspora travellers

For Indian travellers based abroad who combine a Japan holiday with a trip home, the Delhi hub timing creates a practical option: arrive in Delhi on an Air India international flight, connect on AI360 that night, and wake up in Osaka the next morning. Before booking, check your visa position early — Indian residents can review eligibility on the official JAPAN eVISA page from Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which covers the single-entry short-term tourism eVISA for residents of India.

What to watch next is straightforward. Fares for the new route, how quickly all four weekly frequencies are loaded for sale across the full season, and whether demand supports a move toward daily service will show how strongly the Delhi-Osaka market performs after the February 2027 launch.
